title: Advancing a loop head
statement: Let $c,C,q\in\mathbb{N}$, let $x$ be a bit string, let $h:\{0,\ldots,c\}\to\mathbb{Z}$ be a head-position function, let $o$ be an output word, and let $i\in\{0,\ldots,c\}$. One step of the unary box-enumeration machine from the configuration on input $x$ in state $\mathrm{advance}_i$, with tape contents $1^q$ and head positions $h$, reaches the configuration in state $\mathrm{loop}_i$ with the same tape contents and output, and with head positions equal to $h$ except that head $i$ is at $h(i)+1$.
hypotheses_covered: $h$ assigns integer head positions to indices $0,\ldots,c$
replaced: Let $c, C, q \in \mathbb{N}$, $x$ a bit string, $h \colon \{0,\dots,c\} \to \mathbb{Z}$, $o$ an output word and $i \in \{0,\dots,c\}$. One step of $\mathcal{P}_{c,C}$ from $\Gamma_q(\mathrm{advance}_i, h, o)$ yields $\Gamma_q(\mathrm{loop}_i, h[i \mapsto h(i)+1], o)$; here $\mathcal{P}_{c,C}$ is the unary box-enumeration machine with $c+1$ work tapes, which writes $1^{|x|+1}$ on every work tape and then runs $c+1$ nested unary loops, emitting $C$ ones per innermost iteration, and $\mathrm{loop}_i$, $\mathrm{rewind}_i$, $\mathrm{advance}_i$, $\mathrm{emit}_j$ are its control states, $\Gamma_q(s,h,o)$ denotes its configuration on input $x$ in control state $s$, with the input head on the blank cell right of the input, every work tape holding $1^q$ in cells $0,\dots,q-1$ and blanks elsewhere, work head $k$ at position $h(k)$, and output $o$, and $h[i \mapsto v]$ is $h$ with its $i$-th entry replaced by $v$.
